title: Simultaneous compactification of a proper correspondence diagram
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X,Y,C,B$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $c_i:C\to X$, $b_i:B\to Y$ ($i=1,2$) be $k$-morphisms, and let $p:X\to Y$, $q:C\to B$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $b_iq=pc_i$. There exist proper finite-type $k$-schemes $X^*,Y^*,C^*,B^*$, dense open immersions $u_X:X\hookrightarrow X^*$, $u_Y:Y\hookrightarrow Y^*$, $u_C:C\hookrightarrow C^*$, $u_B:B\hookrightarrow B^*$ [def-weil-open-immersion], proper maps $p^*:X^*\to Y^*$, $q^*:C^*\to B^*$, and maps $c_i^*:C^*\to X^*$, $b_i^*:B^*\to Y^*$ such that
$$p^*u_X=u_Yp,\quad q^*u_C=u_Bq,\quad c_i^*u_C=u_Xc_i,\quad b_i^*u_B=u_Yb_i,\quad b_i^*q^*=p^*c_i^*.$$
Here dense means topologically dense. Moreover the squares $(u_X,p,u_Y,p^*)$ and $(u_C,q,u_B,q^*)$ are Cartesian: the natural maps $X\to X^*\times_{Y^*}Y$ and $C\to C^*\times_{B^*}B$ are isomorphisms. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed on the original leg squares, and no original scheme is required to be proper over $k$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), final paragraph, using the graph-closure construction of Remark 1.1.3; Cartesian restriction squares follow from properness and density
